BURHAN:v3p365/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p365/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p365/r6.claim: The feminine verb with masculine مثقال is licensed because مثقال is annexed to the feminine حبة and takes its gender from that noun.
BURHAN:v3p365/r6.anchor: فأنث الفعل المسند ل مثقال وهو مذكر ولكن لما أضيف إلى حبة اكتسب منه التأنيث

BURSEVI:v7p61/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61/r3.claim: The feminine “it” refers to a deed, whether sinful or good.
BURSEVI:v7p61/r3.anchor: أي : الخصلة من الإساءة أو الإحسان

BURSEVI:v7p61/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BURSEVI:v7p61/r4.claim: Luqman's son asked how God would know of a sin committed where no one could see him; Luqman answered that even the mustard-seed deed is known to God.
BURSEVI:v7p61/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل وذلك أن ابن لقمان قال لأبيه : يا أبتاه إن عملت

MAJAZ:v2p127/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p127/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p127/r3.claim: مثقال حبة من خردل means the weight of a mustard seed.
MAJAZ:v2p127/r3.anchor: «يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل» (16) أي زنة حبة

NAHHAS:v3p283/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r9.claim: The feminine pronoun إنها may refer to the story, the deed, or the question the son asked; Basrans allow the “story” construction, while Kufans restrict it to feminine nouns.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r9.anchor: الكتابة عن القصة أو عن الفعلة أو بمعنى إن التي سألتني عنها لأنه يروى أنه سأله

NAHHAS:v3p283/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r10.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v3p283/r10.claim: Abu Hatim considers a nominative مثقال after أن تك impossible because the noun is masculine; al-Nahhas says it is valid by meaning agreement, as in اجتمعت أهل اليمامة.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r10.anchor: واستبعد أبو حاتم أن يقرأ ( أن تك مثقال حبة ) بالرفع لأن مثقالا مذكر

NAHHAS:v3p283/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r11.claim: The agreement is valid by sense, as when Arabic says اجتمعت أهل اليمامة because أهل shares the feminine place-name’s meaning.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r11.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا جائز صحيح وهو محمول على المعنى لأن المعنى واحد

NAHHAS:v3p285/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p285/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p285/r1.claim: Al-Farra cites an anonymous line about speech spreading like blood staining a spear shaft as a parallel to the verse’s sense-based agreement.
NAHHAS:v3p285/r1.anchor: وتشرق بالقول الذي قد أذعته … كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r1.claim: Something's coming to God implies it is accessible; symbolically, knowing and extracting a mustard seed from remote depths in solid rock requires exact knowledge of its location and means.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r1.anchor: والإتيان كناية عن التمكن منها ، وهو أيضا كناية رمزية عن العلم بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r2.claim: إن الله لطيف خبير may be Luqman's conclusion from the example and is syntactically detached because a conclusion follows its proof; it may alternatively be God's parenthetical teaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r2.anchor: وجملة { إن الله لطيف خبير } يجوز أن تكون من كلام لقمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r3.claim: لطيف describes one who knows minute things and reaches them gently; after God's ability to bring a hidden seed, it signals precise knowledge, power, and intact creation, completing core beliefs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r3.anchor: واللطيف : من يعلم دقائق الأشياء ويسلك في إيصالها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.claim: These readers double the yāʾ and give it kasra in the three occurrences of yā bunayya; Hafs and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿAsim double it with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.speaker: ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير وقنبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Barra reports Ibn Kathir with a silent yāʾ in the first occurrence, kasra in the second, and fatḥa in the third; Qunbul reports silence in the first and third and kasra in the second.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير «يا بني» بسكون الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.claim: Luqman uses this example to teach his son the extent of God's power, using a mustard seed so tiny that human senses cannot weigh it, though God encompasses it in knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r1.anchor: المعنى وقال لقمان يا بني، وهذا القول من لقمان إنما قصد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.claim: The tiny measure may describe a physical object or a deed; the apparent sense is a hidden thing, supported by a report that the son asked about a seed lost in the ocean.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه أراد شيئا من الأشياء خفيا قدر حبة، ويؤيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r3.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r3.claim: Many commentators take the mustard seed as sins and acts of obedience; this makes the admonition both hopeful and frightening, since nothing escapes God's bringing it forth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r3.anchor: وذكر كثير من المفسرين أنه أراد الأعمال المعاصي والطاعات، ويؤيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r4.claim: On the physical-object reading, the verse displays God's power but does not itself threaten or encourage reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r4.anchor: وفي القول الآخر ليس ترجية ولا تخويف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r5.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r5.claim: He reads fatakun with kasra on kāf and a doubled nūn, from kann, a covered thing, supporting the concrete-object interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r5.anchor: ومما يؤيد قول من قال هي من الجواهر قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري «فتكن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r6.claim: The majority read in tak with feminine tāʾ and mathqāla accusative as kāna's predicate, supplying an implied subject such as a matter, sin, or act of obedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «إن تك» بالتاء من فوق «مثقال» بالنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r7.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r7.claim: Nafiʿ alone reads mathqālu nominative, taking kāna as a complete verb; its feminine marker agrees with the feminine noun to which mathqāl is annexed, as the cited poetry illustrates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p350#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده بالتاء أيضا «مثقال» بالرفع على اسم «كان»

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.claim: Luqman tells his son that wisdom can seat the poor among kings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.anchor: يا بني، إن الحكمة أجلست المساكين مجالس الملوك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.claim: Luqman advises greeting people at a gathering, sitting quietly until they speak, joining if they remember God, and leaving if their talk turns elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.anchor: ثم اجلس في ناحيتهم، فلا تنطق حتى تراهم قد نطقوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.claim: Luqman illustrates the force of his advice by taking one mustard seed from a bag with each admonition until the bag is empty; the mountain would have split from the counsel, and his son did so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.anchor: لقد وعظتك موعظة لو وعظها جبل لتفطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet names Luqman, the Negus, and Bilal among three distinguished Black figures; al-Ṭabarānī explains that Abyssinians are meant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الطبراني: أراد الحبش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.claim: A report says a poor man in two worn garments may pass unrecognized at people's doors, yet if he swears by God, God fulfills his oath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.anchor: رب أشعث ذي طمرين يصفح عن أبواب الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.claim: A report calls the pious wealthy who are unnoticed when present and unmissed when absent lamps purified from every dark, disgraceful trial.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.anchor: طوبى للأتقياء الأثرياء الذين إذا حضروا لم يعرفوا، وإذا غابوا لم يفتقدوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.claim: Muʿādh tells ʿUmar that even slight showing off is shirk and that God loves discreet, pious, wealthy people who are lamps of guidance and escape dark trials.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.anchor: إن اليسير من الرياء شرك، وإن الله يحب الأتقياء الأخفياء الأثرياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.claim: The Prophet says an unregarded man in worn clothes may have his oath fulfilled by God; if he asks for Paradise, God gives it, though He gives him nothing of worldly status.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.anchor: لو قال: اللهم إني أسألك الجنة لأعطاه الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.claim: A report says some Muslims are ignored by people if they ask for money but granted Paradise if they ask God; God neither gives them worldly goods nor withholds them because He despises them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.anchor: لم يعطه إياها، ولم يمنعها إياه لهوانه عليه

JISHUMI:v8p5653/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r1.speaker: نافع
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ reads “the weight of a grain” in the nominative, either as the subject of kāna without a predicate or with kāna treated as inactive; the others use the accusative as its predicate.
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع: مثقال حبة بالرفع على أنه اسم (كان)

JISHUMI:v8p5653/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r5.claim: Mithqāl is an equivalent weight, from th-q-l, and in “weight of an atom” means its weight; the cited poetry uses mithqāl in the sense of a weight.
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r5.anchor: مثقال ذرة، أي: زنته وثقله، قال الشاعر: وكلا نوافيه الجزاء بمثقال

JISHUMI:v8p5653/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r8.claim: The pronoun in “innahā” is explained either as an emphatic or anticipatory pronoun awaiting the clause that interprets it.
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r8.anchor: الأول: أنها عماد الضمير على شريطة التفسير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r1.claim: The mustard-seed parable concerns even a tiny deed of good or evil; Qatada supplies both kinds of deed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r1.anchor: مثل مضروب لمثقال حبة من خردل . قال قتادة : من خير أو شر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r2.claim: They identify the rock as the one beneath the seventh earth; Ibn al-Harith places it on the fish's back, while Sufyan reports that the sky's greenness comes from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r2.anchor: أنها الصخرة التي تحت الأرض السابعة قاله الربيع بن أنس والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r3.claim: He says the rock is neither in heaven nor on earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس هذه الصخرة ليست في السماء ولا في الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r4.claim: Another view identifies the rock with Sijjin, where the deeds of unbelievers are recorded and not raised to heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r4.anchor: هذه الصخرة هي سجين التي يكتب فيها أعمال الكفار ولا ترفع إلى السماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r5.claim: He takes the rock simply to mean a mountain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r5.anchor: معنى قوله في صخرة أي في جبل , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r6.claim: God will bring the tiny deed forth either by requiting an equivalent good or evil, or by knowing and later recompensing it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r6.anchor: بجزاء ما وازنها من خير أو شر . الثاني : يعلمها الله فيأتي بها إذا شاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r7.claim: He explains لطيف as able to extract the hidden deed and خبير as knowing where it is.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r7.anchor: لطيف } باستخراجها . { خبير } بمكانها , قاله الربيع بن أنس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r8.speaker: علي بن رباح اللخمي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r8.claim: He recounts that Luqman dropped a mustard seed into the sea, later recalled it, and God sent a fly to retrieve it and place it in his hand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r8.anchor: روى علي بن رباح اللخمي قال : لما وعظ لقمان ابنه بهذا أخذ حبة من خردل

MUQATIL:31:16-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r1.claim: Even a mustard seed’s weight hidden in a hollow green rock beneath the earth, in heaven, or anywhere on earth is brought by God; He subtly retrieves it and knows its location.
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r1.anchor: وهي خضراء مجوفة لها ثلاث شعب على لون السماء،

TABATABAI:31:15-17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r3.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to a good or evil deed; even a mustard-seed-sized deed hidden inside rock, heaven, or earth will be brought for judgment, since God knows every hidden thing.
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r3.anchor: والمراد بكونها في صخرة اختفاؤها بالاستقرار في جوف الصخرة الصماء أو في السماوات أو في الأرض

TABATABAI:31:15-17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r4.claim: Luqman's preceding lesson concerned monotheism and denying partners; this verse begins a second lesson about resurrection and the accounting of deeds.
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r4.anchor: كان الفصل السابق من كلامه المنقول راجعا إلى التوحيد ونفي الشريك وما في هذه الآية فصل ثان في المعاد

TABRISI:31:16-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-20/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة
TABRISI:31:16-20/r1.claim: Medinan readers use nominative mithqālu ḥabbatin; the others use the accusative.
TABRISI:31:16-20/r1.anchor: { مثقال حبة } بالرفع وقراءة الباقين بالنصب

TABRISI:31:16-20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-20/r4.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
TABRISI:31:16-20/r4.claim: A non-canonical reading has fa-takin with kasra on the kāf.
TABRISI:31:16-20/r4.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري فتكن في صخرة بكسر الكاف

TABRISI:31:16-20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-20/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:31:16-20/r6.claim: Nominative mithqālu agrees with the semantic feminine of the measured good or evil deed, as in the cited verse; accusative instead makes the injustice, sin, or good deed the subject weighed by God.
TABRISI:31:16-20/r6.anchor: بالرفع فألحق علامة التأنيث بالفعل فلأن المثقال هو السيئة أو الحسنة

TABRISI:31:16-20/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-20/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-20/r12.claim: A person's deed, good or evil, may weigh as little as a mustard seed; the pronoun in inna-hā may instead be a pronoun of the matter.
TABRISI:31:16-20/r12.anchor: معناه أن فعلة الإنسان من خير أو شر إن كانت مقدار حبة خردل

TABRISI:31:16-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:31:16-18/r1.claim: Zajjaj relates that Luqman's son asked whether God would know a seed deep in the sea; Luqman answered that even a mustard seed in a rock, heaven, or earth would be known and brought by God.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r1.anchor: يروى أن ابن لقمان سأل لقمان فقال: أرأيت الحبة تكون في مقل البحر

TABRISI:31:16-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:31:16-18/r2.claim: The rock may be a mountain, a great boulder that hides the tiny seed and makes it hard to retrieve.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r2.anchor: فتكن تلك الحبة في جبل عن قتادة والمعنى في صخرة عظيمة

TABRISI:31:16-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r3.claim: Mentioning heaven and earth after a rock reinforces the point even though the rock must be within earth, as the Qur'an similarly repeats creation and then specifies humankind.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r3.anchor: ذكر السماوات والأرض بعد ذكر الصخرة وإن كان لا بد وإن تكون الصخرة في الأرض على وجه التأكيد

TABRISI:31:16-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r4.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:31:16-18/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says this rock lies below seven earths, a view the author rejects as unworthy of acceptance.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r4.anchor: هذه الصخرة ليست في السماوات ولا في الأرض هي تحت سبع أرضين وهذا قول مرغوب عنه

TABRISI:31:16-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r5.claim: God brings the deed on Judgment Day and requites a good or evil act of corresponding weight.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r5.anchor: يحضِرها الله يوم القيامة ويجازي عليها أي يأت بجزاء ما وازنها من خير أو شر

TABRISI:31:16-18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r6.claim: Alternatively, bringing it means God knows the hidden seed and can manifest it whenever He wills, like the promise that whoever does an atom's weight of good or evil will see it.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r6.anchor: يعلمها الله فيأتي بها إذا شاء كذلك قليل العمل من خير أو شر يعلمه الله فيجازي عليه

TABRISI:31:16-18/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:31:16-18/r7.claim: A report urges avoiding minor sins because they have a pursuer, warning against dismissing them on the grounds that one can repent later.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r7.anchor: اتقوا المحقرات من الذنوب فإن لها طالبا لا يقولن أحدكم أذنب وأستغفر الله

TABRISI:31:16-18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:31:16-18/r8.claim: God is subtle in extracting the hidden deed and knows where it is; another explanation says al-Laṭīf knows hidden matters and al-Khabīr knows everything.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r3.claim: In Luqman’s story, his son asks how God knows a hidden sin; even mustard-seed-sized evil in a rock, heaven, or earth is brought forth for recompense, since God subtly extracts it and knows its location.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r1.claim: A report says the rock is the one on which the whale rests and which supports the earths.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r2.claim: Luqman warns that God will account for a mustard-seed-sized deed wherever found, and knows its location; He is subtle in bringing it forth and knowledgeable of its place.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r1.claim: Luqman's advice grows from his God-given wisdom; awareness that God knows every deed and will reckon it grounds moral responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r1.anchor: Allah’ın mutlaka onu bildiği, dolayısıyla onun hesabını soracağı inancı ve bilinci ile bundan doğan sorumluluk duygusu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r2.speaker: meşhur özdeyiş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r2.claim: A well-known saying identifies fear of God as the beginning of wisdom.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r3.speaker: Mehmed Âkif
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r3.claim: His couplet says virtue in people comes from fear of God, rather than knowledge or conscience alone.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r3.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r3.claim: He reads فتكن with kasra on kāf, from a bird settling in its nest or roost; the author links the root to dwelling and stability and cites poetry about birds in their nests.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري1:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r2.claim: After forbidding shirk, Luqman points to God’s power: nothing within His power can escape or be delayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r2.anchor: ولما نهى لقمان ابنه عن الشرك، نبهه على قدرة الله، وأنه لا يمكن أن يتأخر عن مقدوره شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r3.claim: The pronoun in “it” most naturally refers to the whole matter; Nafi reads “weight” in the nominative, while the other seven make it accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في إنها ضمير القصة. وقرأ نافع: مثقال، بالرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r4.claim: The nominative reading makes the verb complete; the masculine “weight” is treated as feminine because it is annexed to a feminine noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r4.anchor: على إن تك تامة، وهي قراءة الأعرج وأبي جعفر، وأخبر عن مثقال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r5.claim: The accusative reading makes the verb incomplete, with an implied subject; a report says Luqman asked whether God knows a grain at the bottom of the sea.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r5.anchor: وباقي السبعة: بالنصب على إن تك ناقصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r6.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r6.claim: Abd al-Karim al-Jazari has a reading of “it lies” with a kasra on kāf and a doubled, open nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الكريم الجزري: فتكن، بكسر الكاف وشد النون وفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r7.speaker: محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Abi Fajja al-Baʿlabakki reads the verb with ḍamma on tāʾ and a doubled open nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r7.anchor: وقراءة محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي: فتكن، بضم التاء وفتح الكاف والنون مشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r8.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r8.claim: Qatada reads the verb from “to nest or settle”; the same reading is also transmitted from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r8.anchor: وقرأ قتادة: فتكن، بفتح التاء وكسر الكاف وسكون النون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r9.claim: The pronoun may refer to a concrete thing or to an act of obedience or disobedience; on the accusative reading it may refer to the deed itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير ضمير عرض، أي تلك الفعلة من الطاعة أو المعصية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the deed, tiny as a mustard seed and hidden in a rock or anywhere in the universe, will be brought forth for judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فمن نصب يعني مثقال، كان الضمير للهيئة من الإساءة والإحسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r11.claim: God is subtle because His knowledge reaches every hidden thing, and expert because He knows its full reality; Qatada adds that He extracts it and knows its location.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r11.anchor: إن الله لطيف، يتوصل علمه إلى كل خفي. خبير: عالم بكنهه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r12.claim: The examples move from a hard-to-extract rock to distant heavens and then the familiar earth, building toward the most comprehensive sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r12.anchor: وبدأ له بما يتعلق به أولا، وهو كينونة الشيء. في صخرة: وهو ما صلب من الحجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi identify the rock as the one beneath the earth; Ibn Abbas says it lies under the seven earths and records sinners’ deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p414/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والسدي، أن هذه الصخرة هي التي عليها الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the rock lies beneath the seven earths and records the deeds of wicked people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي تحت الأرضين السبع، يكتب فيها أعمال الفجار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports claims about a rock supporting earth, fish, and water on an angel, or a rock in the wind, but says their chains are weak; the language instead expresses maximal scope.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قيل: أراد الصخرة التي عليها الأرض والحوت والماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r3.claim: The rock, heavens, and earth evoke concealment, distance, and darkness; bringing the grain forth demonstrates God’s knowledge and power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r3.anchor: ففي صخرة إشارة إلى الحجاب، وفي السموات إشارة إلى البعد، وفي الأرض إشارة إلى الظلمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r1.claim: The mustard seed illustrates how small a good or bad deed may be; Nafi raises mithqālu as an event pronoun with kāna complete, with feminine agreement explained by annexation or meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r1.anchor: أي أن الخصلة من الإحسان أو الإساءة إن تك مثلا في الصغر كحبة الخردل. ورفع نافع { مثقال }

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r2.claim: A deed in a rock, heaven, or earth is in a concealed, protected, highest, or deepest place; a kasra reading derives from a bird settling in its nest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r2.anchor: في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف صخرة أو أعلاه كمحدب السموات أو أسفله كمقعر الأرض. وقرىء بكسر الكاف

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r3.claim: God brings the deed forth and accounts for it; He is subtle because His knowledge reaches every hidden thing and expert because He knows its essence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r3.anchor: يحضرها فيحاسب عليها. { إن الله لطيف } يصل علمه إلى كل خفي. { خبير } عالم بكنهه.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r2.claim: The affectionate ‘my son’ also stresses how insignificant a child is beside bearing God’s wrath; the feminine pronoun can refer to an act, or to obedience, disobedience, good, or evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r2.anchor: متحببا مستعطفا , مصغرا له بالنسبة إلى حمل شيء من غضب الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r3.claim: The majority read miṯqāla ḥabbatin min khardalin with khardal accusative; the two Medinan readers raise it, construing the clause as the existence of some tiny thing at some time.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r4.claim: Dropping the nūn in in tak emphasizes brevity and the tiniest possible existence; retaining it in fa-takun stresses the deed’s persistence in its location.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r4.anchor: وأسقط النون لغرض الإيجار في الإيصاء بما ينيل المفاز

BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r5.claim: The mustard seed is the least thing likely to come to mind; even if hidden in any rock, across the immense heavens, or anywhere on earth, God brings it forth. Repeated aw marks each realm individually without excluding overlap.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p18/r5.anchor: أي صخرة كانت ولو أنها أشد الصخور وأقواها وأصغرها وأخفاها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r1.claim: God brings even the hidden tiny deed itself into account; His subtle reach and exhaustive knowledge explain why nothing can escape Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r1.anchor: بعظم جلاله , وباهر كبريائه وكماله , بعينها لا يخفى عليه

DURR-FULL:v6p523/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r1.claim: God brings even a mustard-seed-sized deed to light; Abu Malik glosses 'يأت بها الله' as God knowing it.
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله عنه {يأت بها الله} قال: يعلمها الله

DURR-FULL:v6p523/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r2.claim: God is subtle in extracting the tiny deed and knowing where it is settled.
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الله لطيف} قال: باستخراجها قال: بمستقرها

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r1.claim: After Luqman says God will inform people of their deeds (31:15), his son may think secret actions are hidden; Luqman teaches that even an infinitesimal hidden deed is known to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r1.anchor: وقع لابنه أن ما يفعل في خفية يخفي

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r2.claim: Even a good or bad deed as small as a mustard seed remains known to God when concealed in a secure place such as a rock.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r2.anchor: وتكون مع ذلك الصغر في موضع حريز كالصخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r3.claim: The fa in fatakun indicates connection and combination: the seed is tiny and, together with that smallness, is hidden in a secure place, yet God knows it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r3.anchor: بالفاء لإفادة الاجتماع يعني إن كانت صغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r4.claim: Some commentators say the rock is the rock on which the bull rests, located neither in heaven nor on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r4.anchor: ما قاله بعض المفسرين وهو أن المراد بالصخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains an ellipsis: the sense is a rock or another place in the heavens or on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r5.anchor: ما قاله الزمخشري وهو أن فيه إضمارا تقديره

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r6.claim: Al-Razi’s third answer is that a specific item may precede a general category, but the reverse is awkward; he illustrates this with naming houses of Zayd and Amr and then elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r6.anchor: تقديم الخاص وتأخير العام في مثل هذا التقسيم جائز

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r7.claim: The sequence covers four sources of concealment: tiny size, a barrier, great distance in the heavens, and darkness inside the earth; God’s knowledge and disclosure apply despite all four.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r7.anchor: فأثبت الله الرؤية والعلم مع انتفاء الشرائط

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r8.claim: Saying God brings the deed forth is stronger than merely saying He knows it: God displays it to witnesses, joining knowledge with the ability to manifest it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r8.anchor: من يظهر له الشيء ولا يقدر على إظهاره لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r9.claim: Latif means that God’s power penetrates all things; khabir means that He knows their hidden realities.
RAZI-FULL:v25p129#3/r9.anchor: أي نافذ القدرة { خبير } أي عالم ببواطن الأمور

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that if knowledge of an attribute is necessary, knowledge of its bearer must be necessary too; knowing necessarily that God assigned words to meanings would then undermine moral responsibility.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r1.anchor: خلافا للمعتزلة واحتجوا بأن العلم بالصفة إذا كان ضروريا كان العلم بالموصوف أيضا ضروريا

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi answers that God could create necessary knowledge that someone assigned a word to a meaning without creating knowledge that the assigner was God, removing the objection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r2.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال إنه تعالى يخلق علما ضروريا في القلب بأن واضعا وضع هذا اللفظ لهذا المعنى من غير أن يخلق العلم بأن ذلك الواضع هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r3.claim: Because the proofs are weak, al-Razi allows that all languages may be divinely instituted, all conventional, or partly one and partly the other.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r3.anchor: جوزنا أن تكون كل اللغات توقيفية وان تكون كلها اصطلاحية وأن يكون بعضها توقيفيا وبعضها اصطلاحيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r4.claim: A single word cannot initially convey its referent: knowing its assignment requires knowing the relation between word and meaning, which presupposes both and would make learning the meaning from the word circular.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r4.anchor: اللفظ المفرد لا يفيد البتة مسماه لأنه ما لم يعلم كون تلك اللفظة موضوعة لذلك المعنى لم يفد شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi answers the circularity objection by proposing that an established imaginative association lets hearing a particular word call its meaning to mind.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r5.anchor: إذا استقر في الخيال مقارنة بين اللفظ المعين والمعنى المعين فعند حصول الشعور باللفظ ينتقل الخيال إلى المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r6.claim: The circularity problem does not apply to compounds: individual words signify by convention, but reason analyzes their arrangement and reaches the compound meaning through rational relations.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r6.anchor: الإشكال المذكور في المفرد غير حاصل في المركب ؛ لأن إفادة الألفاظ المفردة لمعانيها إفادة وضعية أما التركيبات فعقلية

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r7.claim: Words signify mental meanings rather than external things: as perception changes an object may be named first a rock, then a bird, then a human; the names track changing conceptions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r7.anchor: أنا إذا رأينا جسما من البعد وظنناه صخرة قلنا إنه صخرة فإذا قربنا منه وشاهدنا حركته وظنناه طيرا قلنا إنه طير

RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r8.claim: If words signified external reality, saying both that the world is eternal and that it originated would make it simultaneously both; as mental judgments, the two claims can coexist without contradiction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p30#2/r8.anchor: اللفظ لو دل على الموجود الخارجي لكان إذا قال إنسان العالم قديم وقال آخر العالم حادث لزم كون العالم قديما حادثا معا

STUDYQURAN:31:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r1.claim: Even the smallest good or evil deed will be brought forth and accounted for on the Day of Judgment, as 99:7–8 teaches.
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r1.anchor: All deeds, no matter how small, will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:31:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r2.claim: The verse's mustard-seed image also indicates that all deeds will be weighed on the Day of Resurrection, with no soul wronged.
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r2.anchor: Thus it is said that all deeds will be weighed, as in 21:47

STUDYQURAN:31:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r3.claim: God is Subtle because He knows the minutest details, and Aware because He knows all things at every moment.
STUDYQURAN:31:16/r3.anchor: Subtle indicates that God has knowledge of the minutest details, while Aware indicates that He is aware of all things at every moment

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r1.claim: Takun originally has a wāw, dropped at the meeting of two quiescent letters after the conditional particle removes the nūn's vowel.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r1.anchor: أصله تكون حذفت الواو لاجتماع الساكنين الحاصل من سقوط حركة النون بأن الشرطية

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r2.claim: The nūn is also omitted, likened to a weak letter, nasal wāw, or tanwīn.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r2.anchor: وحذفت النون أيضا تشبيها بحرف العلة في امتداد الصوت أو بالواو في الغنة أو بالتنوين

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r3.claim: Some attribute nūn deletion to easing through frequent use; it is not deleted in lam yaṣun or lam yakhan and returns before a following quiescent letter.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : حذفت تخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال فلا تحذف من مثل لم يصن ولم يخن

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r4.claim: Mithqāl derives from weight and denotes a weighing unit, including any scale weight.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r4.anchor: المثقال ما يوزن به وهو من الثقل وذلك اسم لكل صنج

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r5.claim: Kashf al-Asrār defines a thing's mithqāl as its equivalent in weight, broadened in usage to the measure of the world.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r5.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" يقال : مثقال الشيء ما يساويه في الوزن وكثر الكلام

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r6.claim: The ḥabbah is a seed; mustard is a familiar grain and among the smallest grains used for food.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r6.anchor: والحبة بالفارسية : (دانه) والخردل من الحبوب معروف

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r7.claim: The phrase means an amount as small as the least unit used for weighing, comparable to a mustard seed.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى مقدار ما هو أصغر المقادير التي توزن بها الأشياء من جنس الخردل

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r8.claim: The rock is hard stone, and the image places the tiny thing in an extremely hidden, secure location, such as its interior.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r8.anchor: الصخر الحجر الصلب أي : في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف صخرة ما

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r9.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r9.claim: Jāmī calls the rock the hardest compound and most resistant to extracting what is inside.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r9.anchor: وقال المولى الجامي في صخرة هي أصلب المركبات وأشدها منعا لاستخراج ما فيها

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r10.claim: The indefinite form means any rock whatever.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r10.anchor: والمراد بالصخرة أية صخرة كانت لأنه قال بلفظ النكرة

BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates a cosmic support sequence: earth rests on a fish, then water, a slab, an angel, and a rock; Luqmān's rock is neither in heaven nor on earth.
BURSEVI:v7p61#2/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الأرض على الحوت والحوت في الماء والماء على صفاة

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r1.speaker: بعض التفاسير
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r1.claim: Some commentaries take the heavens as the upper world, for example the convex surface of the heavens.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r1.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير في العالم العلوي كمحدب السموات

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r2.speaker: بعض التفاسير
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r2.claim: Some commentaries take the earth as the lower world, for example its concave surface.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r2.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير في العالم السفلي كمقعر الأرض

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r3.claim: God brings the hidden deed forth for reckoning; this is linked to 99:7–8, and the bāʾ marks causation.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r3.anchor: أي : يحضرها فيحاسب عليها لأنه من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r4.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r4.claim: Jāmī says Nafiʿ reads takun with nominative mithqāl: kāna is complete, feminine through annexation to ḥabbah, and yati bihā brings it for nourishment.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r4.anchor: قال المولى الجامي في "شرح الفصوص" : إنها أي : القصة إن تك مثقال حبة بالرفع كما هو قراءة نافع

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r5.claim: Latīf means God's knowledge reaches every hidden thing; knowing this makes one fear exposure and trust Him with what one does not know.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r5.anchor: فإن أحد معاني اللطيف هو العالم بخفيات الأمور ومن عرف أنه العالم بالخفيات يحذر

BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r6.claim: A couplet says no particle is hidden from God's knowledge and that concealed and manifest are alike before Him.
BURSEVI:v7p61#3/r6.anchor: برو علم يك ذره وشيده نيست كه يدا ونهان بنزدش يكيست

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r1.claim: Khabīr means knowing a thing in its full reality.

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r2.speaker: شرح حزب البحر
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r2.claim: Sharḥ Ḥizb al-Baḥr defines khabīr as knowing fine details inaccessible to others except through investigation; awareness of this makes a servant abandon show for sincerity.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r2.anchor: قال في شرح حزب البحر الخبير هو العليم بدقائق الأمور التي لا يتوصل إليها غيره

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r3.claim: God knows heaven and earth, secrets of conscience and thought, and reckons with them whether hidden in the rock of selves, heaven of spirits, or earth of hearts.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r3.anchor: ويحيط بأسرار الضمائر وبطون الخواطر ويحاسب عليها سواء كانت في صخرة النفوس أو في سماء الأرواح

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r4.claim: The verse warns those practicing watchfulness that God knows rare thoughts and hidden movements.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r4.anchor: وفيه تنبيه لأهل المراقبة والتحذير من الملاحظات لاطلاع الحق على نوادر الخطرات وبطون الحركات

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r5.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads innahā as primordial apportionments of provision, human sincerity, and divine gifts.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يا بنى إنهآ} يشير إلى المقسومات الأزلية

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r6.claim: The rock is nonexistence, heavens are form and meaning, and earth is outward form and structure; allotted felicity or misery reaches a person through effort or an unexpected opening.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r6.anchor: أي : صخرة العدم {أو فى السماوات} في الصورة والمعنى {أو فى الأرض}

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r7.claim: God gently brings each person's portion; the servant should trust His promise and generosity while striving in servitude.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r7.anchor: بعباده {خبير} بإتيان ما قسم لهم بلطف ربوبيته فالواجب على العبد أن يثق بوعده

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r8.claim: Some books say these were Luqmān's last words and awe split his spleen, causing his death.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r8.anchor: وفي بعض الكتب إن هذه الكلمة آخر كلمة تكلم بها لقمان فانشقت مرارته من هيبتها فمات

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r9.claim: Bursevī says awe belongs to the elect; Abraham heard his chest boil while praying, and the Prophet experienced it more perfectly.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r9.anchor: هذا الحضور في مقام الهيبة من صفات المقربين. وكان إبراهيم عليه السلام إذا صلى يسمع

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r10.claim: He laments that admonition fails to move us because heedlessness, forgetfulness, and disobedience have overwhelmed us.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r10.anchor: فواعجبا لأمثالنا كيف لا ينجع فينا الوعظ ولا يأخذ بنا معاني اللفظ وليس إلا من الغفلة والنسيان

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r11.claim: A Persian couplet urges the soul to attain Luqmān's rank and let the fire of awe burn within it.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r11.anchor: تا نيابى رتبه لقمانرا آتش هيبت نسوزد جانرا جان عاشق همو روانه بود

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r1.claim: Some Basran grammarians take the pronoun in innahā as referring to a sin or misdeed.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r1.anchor: بني إن المعصية إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r2.claim: Some Kufan grammarians call the pronoun an auxiliary and explain the feminine verb by the intended feminine referent, the mustard seed; an anonymous poetic line illustrates feminine agreement.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: وهذه الهاء عماد. وقال: أنت تك، لأنه يراد بها الحبة

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r3.speaker: صاحب هذه المقالة
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r3.claim: The Kufan analysis permits either accusative or nominative for mithqāl: the nominative is governed by tak, while an indefinite can lack an overt predicate with kāna and its sisters.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r3.anchor: قال صاحب هذه المقالة: يجوز نصب المثقال ورفعه؛ قال: فمن رفع رفعه بتك، واحتملت النكرة أن لا يكون لها فعل

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r4.speaker: صاحب المقالة الأولى
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r4.claim: On the Basran analysis, the accusative makes mithqāl the predicate completing kāna; the nominative treats kāna as not requiring a predicate.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r4.anchor: وأما صاحب المقالة الأولى، فإن نصب مثقال في قوله، على أنه خبر، وتمام كان، وقال: رفع بعضهم فجعلها كان التي لا تحتاج إلى خبر

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the auxiliary-pronoun analysis: God promises recompense for both good and evil deeds, so the pronoun should not refer only to sin.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين بالصواب عندي، القول الثاني: لأن الله تعالى ذكره لم يعد عباده أن يوفيهم جزاء سيئاتهم دون جزاء حسناتهم

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī parses the accusative with an implicit unknown subject in tak, and the nominative with an implicit predicate, roughly “if it be in the place of a mustard-seed weight.”
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r6.anchor: وأما النصب في المثقال، فعلى أن في «تك» مجهولا، والرفع فيه على أن الخبر مضمر، كأنه قيل: إن تك في موضع مثقال حبة

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r7.claim: Mithqāl ḥabbah means the weight of a seed.

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r8.claim: Whatever deed, good or evil, weighs as little as a mustard seed and is hidden in a rock, heaven, or earth, God will bring forth on Resurrection and requite.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r8.anchor: إن الأمر إن تك زنة حبة من خردل من خير أو شر عملته، فتكن في صخرة، أو في السماوات، أو في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r9.claim: Qatāda says the mustard-seed deed may be good or evil.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r9.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل} [لقمان: 16] من خير أو شر

TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r10.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the rock as the green rock that bears the earth.
TAB-FULL:v18p554#3/r10.anchor: وذلك قول روي عن ابن عباس، وقالوا: هي صخرة خضراء

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith reports that the rock is green and lies on the back of a fish.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث، قال: «الصخرة خضراء على ظهر حوت»

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، وعبد الله، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r2.claim: A report through al-Suddī gives a cosmology of earth on a fish, fish in water, water on a slab, slab on an angel, angel on a rock, and rock in wind; Luqmān’s rock is neither heaven nor earth.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن عبد الله، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " خلق الله الأرض على حوت

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r3.claim: Qatāda says the rock means a mountain.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {فتكن في صخرة} [لقمان: 16] أي جبل

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r4.claim: Some interpreters take God’s bringing it forth to mean that God knows it.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r4.anchor: كان بعضهم يوجه معناه إلى يعلمه الله

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī knows no use of “bring it” meaning “know it”; the reading is possible if it means God knows its location, so nothing is hidden from Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r5.anchor: إلا أن يكون قائل ذلك أراد أن لقمان، إنما وصف الله بذلك، لأن الله يعلم أماكنه

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r6.claim: God is subtle in extracting the seed from wherever it is, and fully aware of its location.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r6.anchor: إن الله لطيف باستخراج الحبة من موضعها حيث كانت خبير بموضعها

TAB-FULL:v18p557/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses God as subtle in extracting the seed and knowing where it rests.
TAB-FULL:v18p557/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، " {إن الله لطيف خبير} [لقمان: 16] أي لطيف باستخراجها خبير بمستقرها

THALABI:v7p313/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r13.speaker: بعض النحاة
THALABI:v7p313/r13.claim: Some grammarians take the pronoun to refer to a sin or disobedience; Muqatil relates this to Anʿam's question about hidden sin.
THALABI:v7p313/r13.anchor: قال بعض النحاة: هذه الكناية راجعة إلى الخطيئة والمعصية، يعني: إن المعصية إن تك

THALABI:v7p313/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r14.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p313/r14.claim: Muqatil says Anʿam asked Luqman how God could know a sin committed where no one saw him.
THALABI:v7p313/r14.anchor: يدل عليه قول مقاتل: قال أنعم بن لقمان لأبيه: يا أبة إن عملت بالخطيئة حيث لا يراني أحد كيف يعلمها الله

THALABI:v7p313/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p313/r15.claim: Other grammarians call the pronoun emphatic support and explain its feminine form by reference to the seed, citing a poet.
THALABI:v7p313/r15.anchor: وقال آخرون: هذه الهاء عماد، وإنما أنث لأنه ذهب بها إلى الحبة، كقول الشاعر: ويشرق بالقول الذي قد أذعته … كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدم

THALABI:v7p314/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p314/r1.claim: Accusative miṯqāl is the predicate of kāna; nominative makes it the subject, with an implied sense if it occurs and no stated predicate.
THALABI:v7p314/r1.anchor: ويرفع المثقال وينصب، فالنصب على خبر كان والرفع على اسمها ومجازه: إن تقع وحينئذ لا خبر له

THALABI:v7p314/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p314/r2.claim: Qatadah says the rock is a mountain.
THALABI:v7p314/r2.anchor: فتكن في صخرة قال قتادة: في جبل

THALABI:v7p314/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p314/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas places the rock beneath the seven earths, where the deeds of the wicked are written, and says the sky's greenness comes from it.
THALABI:v7p314/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هي صخرة تحت الأرضين السبع وهي التي يكتب فيها أعمال الفجار، وخضرة السماء منها

THALABI:v7p314/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r4.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v7p314/r4.claim: Al-Suddi describes the earth on fish Nun and a cosmic sequence of water, slab, angel, rock, and wind.
THALABI:v7p314/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: خلق الله الأرض على حوت وهو النون الذي ذكره الله عز وجل في القرآن ن. والقلم والحوت في الماء، والماء على ظهر صفاة

THALABI:v7p314/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p314/r5.claim: God is subtle in extracting the deed and knows its location.
THALABI:v7p314/r5.anchor: يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف باستخراجها خبير عالم بمكانها

THALABI:v7p314/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p314/r6.claim: A book says Luqman's son died from awe at this saying, which became Luqman's final wisdom.
THALABI:v7p314/r6.anchor: ورأيت في بعض الكتب أن لقمان (عليه السلام) قال لابنه: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r1.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r1.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Luqman’s son asked whether God would know a mustard seed hidden in the sea, and Luqman answered with this verse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r2.claim: Muqātil reports that Luqman’s son asked how God could know of a sin committed where no one could see him, and his father replied with the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: قال ابن لقمان لأبيه: يا أبت، إن عملت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the pronoun can refer to the matter Luqman’s son asked about; it can also introduce the following story or proposition, as in إنّها هند قائمة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى إن التي سألتني عنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq also says the phrase may mean that God will bring forth a person’s deed however small it is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p108/r4.anchor: قال: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى إن فعلة الإنسان وإن صغرت يأت بها الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r1.claim: مثقال is read nominative or accusative. In the accusative analysis, an implied subject is a sin, injustice, or evil deed measured as a mustard seed; the feminine verb can also follow a deed’s meaning, as at 6:160.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r1.anchor: مثقال بالرفع والنصب، فمن نصب باسم كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r2.claim: Here تك means تقع, to occur, and has no predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r2.anchor: و {تك} هاهنا بمعنى تقع، ولا خبر له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r3.claim: In one report, Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the rock as beneath the seven earths, where the deeds of sinners are written.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية: يعني: الصخرة التي تحت الأرضين السبع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r4.claim: Muqātil describes the rock as green and hollow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال مقاتل، قال: وهي صخرة خضراء مجوفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith says it is a green rock on the back of the fish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن الحارث: هي صخرة خضراء على ظهر الحوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the rock as the rock on which the earth rests.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي: هي الصخر التي الأرض عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r7.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says the rock is outside the heavens and earth, beneath the seven earths, with an angel standing on it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا قال السدي: هذه ليست في السموات ولا في الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r8.claim: Qatāda interprets the rock as a mountain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: فتكن في صخرة، أي: جبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r9.claim: Though a rock might seem covered by saying in the earth, al-Suddī says this rock lies outside it; repetition and emphasis are also acceptable, as in 96:1–2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r9.anchor: قيل: قد صرح السدي بأن هذه الصخرة ليست في الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r10.claim: Al-Wāḥidī supports the acceptability of this emphasis and repetition by citing the repeated creation statement in 96:1–2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p109/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا قوله: {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} [العلق: 1] ثم قال: {خلق الإنسان من علق}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, also followed by al-Suddi, glosses God bringing the tiny thing as God knowing it; al-Wahidi says this is a meaning rather than an exegesis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يقول يعلمها الله (¬6). وهذا قول السدي (¬7). وهو معنى وليس بتفسير.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq takes the image as the deeds of people: God brings them forth on Judgment Day, when each atom's weight of good or evil is seen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وهذا مثل لأعمال # البلاد (¬1) إن الله -عز وجل- يأت بأعمالهم يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r3.claim: Abu Ali says this establishes that wrongs are hidden from God by none; He will bring them forth and reward or punish for them unless expiation or annulment intervenes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: هذا يثبت أن المظالم لا تخفى عليه، وأن الله تعالى يأت بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and al-Zajjaj explain لطيف as able to extract the hidden thing and خبير as knowing its location.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p110/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل والزجاج: لطيف باستخراجها، خبير بمكانها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r6.claim: “My son” returns to Luqmān’s speech to his son, recalling his earlier exhortation not to associate partners with God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {يا بني} [لقمان: 16] رجع إلى كلام لقمان، يعني:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r7.claim: The phrase means the weight of a mustard seed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p675/r7.anchor: وقوله: {إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل} [لقمان: 16] ، أي: وزن حبة من خردل.

ELMALILI:31:15-16/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r4.claim: The tiny, hidden deed may be good or bad, high or low; God brings it before the person in the afterlife.
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r4.anchor: Allah onu getirir âhirette karşına kor

ELMALILI:31:15-16/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r5.claim: God is Latif because His power reaches the finest and most hidden things, and Khabir because His knowledge encompasses them all.
ELMALILI:31:15-16/r5.anchor: en ince, en gizli şeylere yetişir {خَبِيرٌۭ} ilmi ile hepsini bilir.

BAQILLANI:v1p70/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r1.speaker: الأصمعي وأبو عبيد وحماد وأبو عمرو
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r1.claim: These authorities praise the cited phrase as an unsurpassed instance of bold metaphor.
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r1.anchor: وذكر الأصمعي وأبو عبيد وحماد وقبلهم أبو عمرو أنه أحسن في هذه اللفظة وأنه اتبع فلم يلحق

BAQILLANI:v1p70/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r2.claim: Some critics call this device irdāf: instead of naming the intended meaning directly, the poet names an associated quality, as with staying up late or a long neck.
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r2.anchor: وهوأن يريد الشاعر دلالة على معنى فلا يأتي باللفظ الدال على ذلك المعنى بل بلفظ هو تابع له وردف

BAQILLANI:v1p70/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r3.claim: Critics place the Quranic images of a head kindled with gray hair and lowered wings of humility in the same indirect, allusive figure.
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r3.anchor: ويجعلون من هذا القبيل ما قدمنا ذكره من القرآن

BAQILLANI:v1p70/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r4.claim: Good simile is another badiʿ form; the author says Imruʾ al-Qays achieves accurate division between two sides of a comparison, while Bashshār compares the two clauses without matching each side in detail.
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r4.anchor: وقد سبق امرؤ القيس إلى صحة التقسيم في التشبيه ولم يتمكن بشار إلا من تشبيه إحدى الجملتين بالأخرى

BAQILLANI:v1p70/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p70/r5.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's descriptions of horse ears and eyes are followed by similar lines from Ṭarafah, illustrating poetic imitation of an earlier image.

BURHAN:v1p83/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p83/r1.claim: The Luqman verse exemplifies a closing phrase that fits its subject: God's subtle knowledge reaches even a mustard seed hidden anywhere.
BURHAN:v1p83/r1.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى حكاية عن لقمان ﴿ يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير ﴾

BURHAN:v2p250/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.claim: The twenty-eighth address type is affectionate address, illustrated by Abraham’s gentle يا أبت, Luqman’s يا بني, and Aaron’s يا ابن أم.

BURHAN:v1p407#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r4.claim: The shortened إن تك in Luqman's example likewise marks how minute the seed-sized matter is.
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r4.anchor: إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل

ITQAN:v3p92/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.claim: An affectionate address appears in Abraham's gentle address to his father, Luqmān's address to his son, and Aaron's appeal to Moses; 20:94 is cited as an example.
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.anchor: الحادي والثلاثون خطاب التحبب نحو ﴿ يا أبت لم تعبد ﴾ ﴿ يا بني إنها إن تك ﴾

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r1.claim: Because the eye is indispensable to a lookout’s task, its name can stand for the whole person, as though the eye were the person himself.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r1.anchor: العين لما كانت المقصودة في كون الرجل ربيئة صارت كأنها الشخص كله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r2.claim: Names can transfer through causal relations: rain is treated as the vegetation it produces, while rain is called “sky” because it descends from the sky; such links vary in strength and clarity.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r2.anchor: والغيث لما كان النبت يكون عنه صار كانه هو والمطر لما كان ينزل من السماء عبروا عنه باسمها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r3.claim: Calling the slaughtered sheep an ʿaqīqah has a stronger relation than calling a cry an ʿaqīrah, which arose accidentally; the latter resembles a proverb repeated after the fact, such as “summer, you squandered the milk.”
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r3.anchor: الشاة التي تذبح عن الصبي إذا حلقت عقيقته عقيقة وتجد حالها بعد أقوى من حال العقيرة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r4.claim: Metaphor is broader than istiʿārah: every istiʿārah is a metaphor, but not every metaphor is an istiʿārah.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r4.anchor: أن أبين أن المجاز أعم من الاستعارة وان الصحيح من القضية في ذلك أن كل استعارة مجاز وليس كل مجاز استعارة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو الحسن
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r5.claim: Al-Qadi Abu al-Hasan defines istiʿārah through closeness and affinity of resemblance; al-Jurjani cites this conventional definition to explain its narrower transfer of a name through simile and hyperbole.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p345/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو الحسن في أثناء فصل ذكرها فيه وملاك الاستعارة تقريب الشبه ومناسبة المستعار للمستعار منه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r1.claim: Al-Jurjānī juxtaposes earlier praise with Abū Tammām’s recasting to show how poetic merit can come from reshaping an idea into a more distinctive image.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r1.anchor: فعمد أبو تمام إلى هذا البيت الأخير فقال

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r2.speaker: المرزباني
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r2.claim: Al-Marzubānī explains the old proverb as fearing one harm, escaping it, then suffering an unexpected harm; he gives poetic adaptations, with al-Buḥturī especially praised for expressive power and breadth of meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r2.anchor: قال : ومن الأمثال القديمة قولهم : ' حرا أخاف على جاني كمأة لا قرا ' يضرب مثلا للذي يخاف من شيء ، فيسلم منه ويصيبه غيره مما لم يخفه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r3.speaker: علي بن هارون
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r3.claim: ʿAlī ibn Hārūn says Aḥmad ibn Fannun borrowed Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mahdī’s meaning and wording, yet became more entitled to it through clearer expression and a better approach.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r3.anchor: قال علي بن هارون : أخذه أحمد بن فنن معنى ولفظا فقال ، + الكامل + :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r4.claim: These comparisons show that eloquence is not merely wording: a special image and quality arise in the meaning and are apprehended by reason rather than hearing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p347/r4.anchor: ففي هذا دليل لمن عقل أنهم لا يعنون بحسن العبارة مجرد اللفظ ، ولكن صورة وصفة وخصوصية تحدث في المعنى

DAMGHANI:v1p372/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r13.claim: The entry lists fourteen senses: intercourse, response, nearness, duration, the closest, the most correct, gentleness, kinship, Jerusalem’s Rock, before death, honor, neighboring, and a sacrificial offering.
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r13.anchor: ق ر ب على أربعة عشر وجها القرب الجماع الإجابة مداناة المدة الأقرب الأصوب اللين القربى القرابة صخرة بيت المقدس قبل الموت الكرامة المجاورة القربان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#4/r1.claim: God will reveal or bring it forth; nothing is hidden from Him.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#4/r1.anchor: {يأت بها الله} أي يظهرها الله ولا تخف عليه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r1.claim: Ifk is falsehood because it is speech turned away from truth; afakta al-rajul means that you turned him from an opinion he held.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r1.anchor: الكذب، لأنه كلام قلب عن الحق. وأصله من أفكت الرجل إذا صرفته عن رأي كان عليه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r3.claim: In fa-annā tuʾfakūn, the phrase means “where are you turned away from the truth?”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r3.anchor: قول الله جل وعز: {فأنى تؤفكون} (5) أي: من أين تحرمون وتصرفون عن الحق

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r4.claim: An unnamed poet uses maʾfūkan for someone turned away from the finest beneficence, and says others have likewise been turned away.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p30#4/r4.anchor: مأ ... فوكا ففي آخرين قد أفكوا (6)

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r1.claim: إنها is a pronoun of the matter explained by the conditional clause.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r1.anchor: قوله: { إنها إن تك }: ضمير القصة. والجملة الشرطية مفسرة للضمير.

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r2.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r2.claim: Nafi reads مثقال nominative as subject of complete كان; feminine ت is explained by annexation or its sense of a grain's weight.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r2.anchor: وتقدم أن نافعا يقرأ " مثقال " بالرفع على أن " كان " تامة وهو فاعلها. وعلى هذا فيقال: لم لحقت فعله تاء التأنيث؟

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r3.claim: For accusative مثقال, al-Zamakhshari allows إنها to refer to a tiny good or bad deed.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r3.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري في ضمير " إنها " أن تكون للهنة من السيئات أو الإحسان في قراءة من نصب " مثقال ".

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r4.claim: Another view refers the pronoun to whatever was being asked about.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r4.anchor: وقيل: الضمير يعود على ما يفهم من سياق الكلام أي: إن التي سألت عنها إن تك.

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r5.speaker: التفسير
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r5.claim: A tafsir report says Luqman asked whether God knows a grain falling into the sea's depths.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r5.anchor: وفي التفسير: أنه سأل أباه: أرأيت الحبة تقع في مغاص البحر: أيعلمها الله؟

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r6.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r6.claim: Abd al-Karim al-Jazari reads فتكن with doubled open ن, meaning it settles.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الكريم الجزري " فتكن " بكسر الكاف وتشديد النون مفتوحة أي: فتستقر.

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r7.speaker: محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Abi Fajja al-Ba'labakki has the same vocalization but passive.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r7.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي " فتكن " كذلك إلا أنه مبني للمفعول.

SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r8.speaker: قتادة
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r8.claim: Qatada reads with light ن from وكن, meaning settle in its shelter.
SAMIN-DURR:31:16/r8.anchor: وقتادة " فتكن " بكسر الكاف وتخفيف النون مضارع " وكن " أي: استقر في وكنه ووكره.

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r5.claim: God will bring forth even a mustard seed's weight wherever hidden, including a rock or the depths of the sea, because He knows its location.

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r6.speaker: رواية
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r6.claim: Luqman's son asks whether God knows of a seed in the sea's depths; Luqman explains God knows it in the most hidden place.
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r6.anchor: ويروى أن ابن لقمان سأل لقمان فقال

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r7.claim: مقل يمقل means to dive; a seed inside rock is more hidden than one in water, yet God knows it.

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r8.claim: The seed exemplifies human deeds God brings forth on Judgment Day, like the verses about an atom's weight of good or evil.
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r8.anchor: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره (7) ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره (8)

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r9.claim: Nominative مثقال can accompany feminine تك because it refers in sense to feminine خردلة, as in إن تك حبة.
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r9.anchor: راجع إلى معنى خردلة، فهو بمنزلة إن تك حبة

ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r10.claim: Accusative مثقال can refer to the object asked about or a deed, however small; إنها may refer to the whole matter.
ZAJJAJ:v4p196/r10.anchor: على معنى أن التي سألتني عنها إن تك مثقال حبة

ASAD-NOTES:31:16#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:16#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:16#n17/r1.claim: Asad renders latif as 'unfathomable' and refers readers to his discussion in note 89 on surah 6.
ASAD-NOTES:31:16#n17/r1.anchor: For my rendering of latif as "unfathomable", see surah 6, note 89.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r12.speaker: الزركشي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r12.claim: Al-Zarkashi applies the same principle to a good deed or mustard seed: despite its tiny scale, God multiplies or brings it forth.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r12.anchor: وجاء في (البرهان) للزركشي أن حذف النون في نحو هذا قد يكون "تنبيهاً على صغر مبدأ الشيء وحقارته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r4.claim: In Luqmān 31:16 the nūn is dropped in the first verb because the seed's location is unspecified, then retained in the second after the possible locations are named and delimited.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p650/r4.anchor: الأولى حذفت منها النون لأنه لم يذكر مكان الحبة أما الثانية فذكر فيها النون لأنه ذكر المكان وحدده

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.claim: Luqman’s counsel shows Arabs that their own sages taught what the Qur’an teaches; it contrasts blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan with the wise ancestors’ reflection, and condemns punishing children for conduct Luqman taught his son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.anchor: The succeeding verses refer to the wisdom of Luqmān and the advise he gave to his obedient son.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r1.claim: After God’s inserted parent guidance, Luqmān resumes his counsel: monotheism comes first, followed by the hereafter as the second basic belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r1.anchor: After the intervening verses from God, the counsel of Luqmān resumes from here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r2.claim: Every good or evil deed, however tiny and wherever hidden, will be brought forth on Judgment Day because God is discerning and all-knowing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r2.anchor: God will it bring forth on the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r3.claim: Ignorance of God’s attributes leads nations into errors about monotheism and the hereafter; Luqmān corrects his son’s understanding of both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r3.anchor: It is because of a lack of knowledge about the attributes of God because of which nations have been misled about monotheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r4.claim: The pronoun in “innaha” is ṣamīr al-sha’n, used for something mentally present to the speaker.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r4.anchor: is the pronoun of shā’n. In such situations, a speaker uses a pronoun for a thing in his mind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r5.claim: The pronoun’s referent is the knowledge of a mustard-seed-sized deed, and its feminine form agrees with habba (seed).
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r5.anchor: Here this is antecedent is “knowledge of the size of the mustard seed.” It is in deference to ٍۃَّبَح that the feminine pronoun is used.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r6.claim: The author says ṣakhrah need not mean a stone; it can mean a mountain and its passes, which fits Arabic usage, and he translates accordingly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r6.anchor: It can also refer to a mountain and its passes and this would be in conformity with linguistic principles of Arabic.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r7.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a group that interprets ṣakhrah as a mountain or its passes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p112/r7.anchor: Ṭabarī has also cited that one group of people interpret this word in this meaning.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r1.claim: Nafi reads مثقال nominative; the other readers read it accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده: (إنها إن تك مثقال حبة) [لقمان/ 16] رفعا، ونصب الباقون اللام .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r2.speaker: author
