FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r2.claim: With the accusative, the implied subject is a wrong or deed: if it weighs a mustard seed, God brings it forth and rewards or punishes it unless forgiven or effaced.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r2.anchor: من نصب فقال: إن تك مثقال حبة فاسم كان ينبغي أن تكون: المظلمة، المعنى: إن تك المظلمة أو السيئة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r3.claim: In Nafi's nominative reading, the feminine verb agrees by meaning: مثقال refers to a good or bad deed despite being masculine.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r3.anchor: فألحق علامة التأنيث الفعل، والفاعل مثقال المذكر، فلأن المثقال هو السيئة أو الحسنة فأنث على المعنى

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r4.claim: Mentioning both a rock and the earth reinforces that even a deed hidden in the most inaccessible place cannot escape God's knowledge or recompense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p455#2/r4.anchor: فكذلك وصفت المظلمة بكونها في صخرة أخفى لها، وأغمض لمكانها ففيه تأكيد وتثبيت أن هذه المظالم لا تخفى عليه

NASHR:v2p323/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p323/r4.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p323/r4.claim: The two Medinans put the lām of mithqāl in the nominative in both verses; the other readers use the accusative in both.
NASHR:v2p323/r4.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان برفع اللام في الموضعين

NASHR:v2p289/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p289/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ in all six occurrences; Abū Bakr agrees at the Hūd occurrence, and al-Bazzī agrees at the last Luqmān occurrence, yā bunayya aqimi al-ṣalāh.
NASHR:v2p289/r1.anchor: روى حفص بفتح الياء في الستة

NASHR:v2p289/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p289/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr has no disagreement on the middle Luqmān occurrence: its yāʾ is doubled and kasra-marked; the other readers use that form across all six occurrences.
NASHR:v2p289/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف عنه في كسر الياء مشددة في الحرف الأوسط

QIRAAT-ER:31:16:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:16:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:16:2#1/r1.claim: Kasra rather than fatḥa on the final yāʾ shifts the form from accusative or vocative toward genitive or possessive emphasis.
QIRAAT-ER:31:16:2#1/r1.anchor: Kasra on final yāʾ instead of fatḥa — shifts from accusative/vocative to genitive/possessive emphasis

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the rock as the one on which the earth rests.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله ﴿ فتكن في صخرة ﴾ قال الصخرة التي الأرض عليها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says God will bring forth even a mustard seed’s weight of good or evil wherever it is hidden.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r2.anchor: قال ﴿ أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله ﴾ يقول إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل من خير أو شر يأت بها الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r3.speaker: الثوري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r3.claim: Al-Thawrī locates the rock beneath the earths and says reports attribute the sky’s green color to that rock.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p105#4/r3.anchor: قال الثوري قال صخرة تحت الأرضين قال بلغنا أن خضرة السماء من تلك الصخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r1.claim: The account returns to Luqman's story to give the rest of his counsels after the opening injunction against shirk was reinforced parenthetically.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r1.anchor: رجوع إلى القصة بذكر بقية ما أريد حكايته من وصايا لقمان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r2.claim: The pronoun in إنها refers to a good or bad deed understood from context.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r2.anchor: أي الخصلة من الإساءة والإحسان لفهمها من السياق

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r3.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as the matter the son asked about; a report says he asked whether God knows a mustard seed falling into the depths of the sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r3.anchor: أنها أي التي سألت عنها فقد روى أن لقمان سأله إبنه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r4.claim: The deed may be as tiny as a mustard seed; mithqal is a measure of weight matched by equal weight in common usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r4.anchor: والمثقال ما يقدر به غيره لتساوي ثقلهما وهو في العرف معلوم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r5.speaker: نافع، والأعرج، وأبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r5.claim: Nafi, al-Araj, and Abu Jafar read مثقال in the nominative; the pronoun refers to the clause and تك is complete, with feminine agreement explained by its subject or by interpreting it as weight or a deed.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع والأعرج وأبو جعفر ( مثقال ) بالرفع على أن الضمير للقصة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r6.claim: Even at its tiniest and in a hidden, inaccessible place—the rock's interior, heaven, or earth—God will bring the deed forth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r6.anchor: في أقصى غايات الصغر والقماءة في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r7.claim: Another view specifies the rock's interior, heaven's highest convex surface, or earth's lowest concavity; the author says the wording does not require these extremes, though emphasis may call for them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r7.anchor: في أخفى مكان وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة أو أعلاه كمحدب السموات أو أسفله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r8.claim: في may refer spatially, be used by matching expression, or carry the sense of على to express firm presence; the spatial sense remains strongest.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r8.anchor: ذكرت بحسب المكانية أو للمشاكلة أو هي بمعنى على وعبر بها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan says the order begins with the familiar, hard-to-extract rock, then the more wondrous upper world, then familiar earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r9.anchor: بدأ بما يتعقله السامع أولا وهو كينونة الشيء في صخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r10.claim: One rhetorical account maps the seed's minuteness to tiny size, rock to concealment, heaven to distance, and earth's interior to darkness; no particular rock is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r10.anchor: إن خفاء الشيء وصعوبة نيله بطرق بغاية صغره ويبعده عن الرائي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi identify the rock as the one on which the earth rests.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r11.anchor: وعن إبن عباس والسدي أن هذه الصخرة هي التي عليها الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r12.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas describes the earth resting on Nun, a sea, a green rock, a bull's horn, and moist earth, with only God knowing what lies beneath.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88/r12.anchor: وأخرج إبن مردويه عن إبن عباس أن الأرض على نون والنون على بحر والبحر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r1.claim: Some identify the verse's rock with a cosmological rock in the wind; Ibn Atiyya calls such reports weakly transmitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r1.anchor: قال إبن عطية : وكل ذلك ضعيف لا يثبت سنده

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r2.claim: The strongest reading is hyperbole: God's power reaches inside a rock and anywhere in heaven or earth; the cosmos lies in His grasp, so the cosmological tales should be set aside.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r2.anchor: والأقوى عندي وضع هذه الأخبار ونحوها فليست الأرض إلا في حجر الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r3.speaker: عبدالرحيم الجزري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahim al-Jazari reads فتكن with kasra on kaf and a doubled, open nun.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبدالرحيم الجزري ( فتكن ) بكسر الكاف وشد النون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Abi Fajja al-Baalbakki reads فتكن with damma on ta and a doubled, open nun after fatha on kaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن أبي فجة البعلبكي ( فتكن ) بضم التاء وفتح الكاف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r5.claim: Qatada reads فتكن with fatha on ta, kasra on kaf, and silent nun; the same reading is also reported from al-Jazari.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ( فتكن ) بفتح التاء وكسر الكاف وسكون النون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r6.claim: These readings derive from a bird settling in its nest, used metaphorically or by metonymy; the pronoun refers to the previously mentioned matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r6.anchor: من وكن الطائر إذا أستقر في وكنته أي عشه ففي الكلام إستعارة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r7.claim: A possible alternative makes the pronoun the son: if he hides at reckoning, God brings him forth; the author says this does not fit the answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r7.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للإبن والمعنى إن تختف أو تخف وقت الحساب يحضرك الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r8.claim: God brings the deed forward for reckoning, literally or by making it present as if witnessed through mention and admission.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r8.anchor: أي يحضرها فيحاسب عليها وهذا أما على ظاهره أو المراد يجعلها كالحاضر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r9.claim: Latif means God's knowledge reaches every hidden thing; khabir means He knows its full reality, explaining how He can bring the deed forth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r9.anchor: إن الله لطيف ( يصل علمه تعالى إلى كل خفي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r10.claim: Qatada explains Latif as subtle in extracting the deed and khabir as knowing its location; another gloss calls God kind to servants and aware of hidden things, which the author dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r10.anchor: وعن قتادة لطيف بإستخراجها خبير بمستقرها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r11.speaker: علي بن رباح اللخمي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r11.claim: Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi reports that Luqman threw a mustard seed into the Yarmuk valley, waited, recalled it, and a fly brought it to his palm.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r11.anchor: عن علي بن رباح اللخمي أنه لما وعظ لقمان إبنه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r12.claim: After commanding monotheism by forbidding shirk, Luqman alerts his son to God's complete knowledge and power.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p88#2/r12.anchor: أمره بالتوحيد الذي هو أول ما يجب على المكلف في ضمن النهي عن الشرك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: For one three-letter pattern, a mass or collective noun takes a feminine -ة form for an individual, as in صخر/صخرة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: فأما ما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا فهو نحو طلح والواحدة طلحة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Use the singular with -ات for a small number; for many, use the collective noun itself.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Some such unit nouns also take a broken plural on فعال, as with سخلة/سخال, بهمة/بهام, and طلحة/طلاح.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وربما جاءت الفعلة من هذا الباب على فعال وذلك قولك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Some speakers pluralize صخرة as صخور, by analogy with بدرة/بدور and مأنة/مؤون.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وصخور فجعلت بمنزلة بدرة وبدور ومأنة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: The same unit-and-collective pattern applies to nouns with weak wāw or yāʾ, which show forms such as مرو/مروة, صعوة/صعو/صعاء, and شرية/شري.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Some doubled nouns form unit/collective pairs such as حبة/حب and قتة/قت; a second three-letter pattern likewise forms pairs such as بقرة/بقر and شجرة/شجر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: ما كان على ثلاثة أحرف وكان فعلا فإن قصته كقصة فعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Weak nouns also show variants such as حصى/حصاة/حصيات, قطاة/قطا, and أضاة/أضا/إضاء; Sībawayh says إكام-like forms were analogized to رحاب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: ونظير هذا من بنات الياء والواو حصى وحصاة وحصيات

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Forms such as حلق/حلقة and فلك/فلكة are rare; adding the feminine marker lightens the unit form and changes its meaning.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وقد قالوا حلق وفلك ثم قالوا حلقة وفلكة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Yunus reports Abu Amr's usage of حلقة as an alternative form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وهذا قليل وزعم يونس عن أبي عمر و أنهم يقولون حلقة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: A less frequent pattern has no attested broken plural beyond the collective form; examples include نبقة/نبق and خربة/خرب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: إلا أنا لم نسمعهم كسروا الواحد على بناء سوى الواحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Several other patterns form unit nouns and collectives, usually with regular -ات plurals; Sībawayh gives examples including عنبة/عنب, سمرة/سمر, and بسرة/بسر.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: The word نعر names a disease affecting camels in their heads.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: والنعر داء يأخذ الإبل في رءوسها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: أبو الخطاب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Abu al-Khattab says the singular of طلى is طلاة, with -ات used for a small number; Sībawayh also gives حكأة and مرعة as unit forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب أن واحد الطلى طلاة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Some speakers form a broken plural سدر from سدرة, analogizing it to forms such as لقحة/لقاح and طلحة/طلاح.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: وقد قالوا سدرة وسدر فكسروها على فعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: المسيب بن علس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: Sībawayh cites al-Musayyib ibn Alas's الحقق as poetic attestation for the plural of حقة.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.claim: The same unit-and-collective pattern covers دخنة/دخن and doubled forms such as درة/در, with درر also attested as a broken plural.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانواحدايقعللجميعويكون.anchor: ومثل ذلك من المضاعف در ودرة ودرات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r6.claim: The pronoun “it” refers to a sin; Luqman’s son had asked how God could know of a sin committed where no one saw him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r6.anchor: راجعة إلى الخطيئة، وذلك أن ابن لقمان قال لأبيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r7.claim: Qatada says the rock is a mountain.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas places the rock beneath the seven earths and says it is where the deeds of the wicked are written; the sky’s greenness comes from it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في صخرة تحت الأرضين السبع، وهي التي تكتب فيها أعمال الفجار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r9.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r9.claim: Al-Suddi describes a cosmology in which the earth rests on a fish, the Quranic “Nun,” which is in water; the water rests on a slab, which rests on an angel, then the rock mentioned by Luqman, and the rock rests on the wind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r9.anchor: قال السدي: خلق الله الأرض على حوت -وهو النون الذي ذكر الله عز وجل في القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r10.claim: God can bring the tiny hidden deed forth; “subtle” here means able to extract it, and “aware” means knowing where it is.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r10.anchor: إن الله لطيف} باستخراجها، {خبير} عالم بمكانها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r11.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse expresses God’s encompassing knowledge of things both small and great.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r11.anchor: قال الحسن: معنى الآية هو الإحاطة بالأشياء، صغيرها وكبيرها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r12.claim: A book reports that these were Luqman’s final words; awe made his gall rupture and he died.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p288/r12.anchor: وفي بعض الكتب إن هذه الكلمة آخر كلمة تكلم بها لقمان فانشقت مرارته من هيبتها فمات.

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.claim: In a story whose narrator is not present in this excerpt, Gabriel says God had ordered a city's destruction but spared Luqman and his son because the son's affliction had held them back; Gabriel heals the boy and restores their provisions before carrying them home.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.anchor: قال: أنا جبريل أمرني ربي بخسف هذه المدينة ومن فيها فاخبرت انكما تريدانها

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.speaker: علي بن رباح اللخمي
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.claim: Luqman illustrates that God can retrieve what is hidden: he casts a mustard seed into the broad Yarmuk, waits, then opens his hand and flies bring it back to his palm.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.anchor: عن علي بن رباح اللخمي أنه لما وعظ لقمان عليه السلام ابنه قال: {إنها إن تك}

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.speaker: مالك
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.claim: Luqman says that no wealth compares with health and no blessing compares with a contented disposition.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.anchor: عن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: بلغني أن لقمان عليه السلام قال لابنه: ليس غنى كصحة ولا نعيم كطيب نفس

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.claim: Luqman warns that lying drains a person's dignity and bad character multiplies grief.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه رضي الله عنه قال: قال لقمان عليه السلام لابنه: من كذب ذهب ماء وجهه

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.claim: Luqman says moving rocks from their places is easier than making an unreceptive person understand.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.anchor: ونقل الصخور من مواضعها أيسر من إفهام من لا يفهم

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.claim: Luqman says no burden was heavier than a bad neighbor, despite having carried stone, iron, and other heavy things.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله تعالى عنه أن لقمان قال لابنه: يا بني حملت الجندل والحديد وكل شيء ثقيل

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.claim: Luqman says poverty is more bitter than anything else he has tasted.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.anchor: وذقت المر فلم أذق شيئا هو أمر من الفقر

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.claim: Luqman advises against sending an ignorant messenger; if no wise messenger is available, one should go oneself.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.anchor: لا ترسل رسولك جاهلا فإن لم تجد حكيما فكن رسول نفسك

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.claim: Luqman cautions against lying: it tastes sweet like sparrow meat, but soon turns against its owner.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.anchor: إياك والكذب فإنه شهي كلحم العصفور عما قليل يقلي صاحبه

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.claim: Luqman advises attending funerals rather than weddings because funerals recall the afterlife while weddings stir desire for worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.anchor: احضر الجنائز ولا تحضر العرس فإن الجنائز تذكرك الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.claim: Luqman says not to eat when already full, since giving the excess to a dog would be better than eating it.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.anchor: لا تأكل شبعا على شبع فإنك إن تلقه للكلب خير من أن تأكله

DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.claim: Luqman advises moderation in one's manner: do not be so sweet that people swallow you or so bitter that they spit you out.
DURR-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.anchor: لا تكن حلوا فتبلع ولا مرا فتلفظ

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r8.claim: Qatada says the mustard seed's weight may be of good or evil, and the rock where it is hidden means a mountain.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a cosmology in which the earth rests on a fish, the fish on a sea, the sea on a green rock, the rock on a bull's horn, and the bull on the soil; only God knows what lies below the soil.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: الأرض على نون والنون على بحر والبحر على صخرة خضراء فخضرة الماء من تلك الصخرة

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r10.claim: The report says that at the Resurrection creation vanishes, the heavens and earth tremble, and God answers His own question about sovereignty: it belongs to God, the One, the Overpowering.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r10.anchor: فإذا كان يوم القيامة لم يبق شيء من خلقه قال: {لمن الملك اليوم} فيهتز ما في السموات والأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.claim: Luqman’s counsel warns against associating partners, commands kindness to parents and awareness of God, prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and patience, and rejects pride while urging humility in walking and speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.anchor: من التحذير من الإشراك ، ومن الأمر ببر الوالدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r5.claim: Repeating the vocative renews the listener’s attention for the coming words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r5.anchor: تكرير النداء لتجديد نشاط السامع لوعي الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r6.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r6.claim: Nāfi‘ and Abū Ja‘far read مثقال in the nominative as the subject of complete kāna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو جعفر { إن تك مثقال } برفع { مثقال } على أنه فاعل { تك من ( كان ) التامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r7.claim: In that reading, مثقال takes feminine agreement from its annexed حبة; إنها refers to the event as a feminine pronoun of the matter, a common construction when a feminine term follows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r7.anchor: وإنما جيء بفعله بتاء المضارعة للمؤنثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r8.claim: The pronoun of the matter often follows إن and also serves as the implied subject of lightened أن; it focuses attention on what follows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r8.anchor: ويكثر وقوع ضمير الشأن بعد ( إن )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r9.claim: The call, إن and the pronoun of the matter make three emphatic markers, stressing the danger of the claim and establishing God’s comprehensive knowledge and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p161/r9.anchor: فاجتمع في هذه الجملة ثلاثة مؤكدات : النداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r1.claim: Mentioning the tiniest, most hidden object in an inaccessible place proves that whatever is more visible and near is all the more within God’s knowledge and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r1.anchor: فذكر أدق الكائنات حالا من حيث تعلق العلم والقدرة به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r2.speaker: الباقون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r2.claim: The other readers put مثقال in the accusative as the predicate of defective kāna, supplying its subject from context; إنها then means the deed, good or bad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r2.anchor: وقرأه الباقون بنصب { مثقال } على الخبرية ل { تك } من ( كان ) الناقصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r3.claim: مثقال is an object by which weight is measured, shaped on the pattern of an instrument noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r3.anchor: ما يقدر به الثقل ولذلك صيغ على زنة اسم الآلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r4.claim: A حبة is one seed or grain from a plant, including grain or legume, capable of seeding its kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r4.anchor: واحدة الحب وهو بذر النبات من سنابل أو قطنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r5.claim: Mustard is described as a branching plant with small yellow flowers and tiny, sharply pungent seeds; its seeds were widely used in medicinal poultices for internal inflammation, though physicians increasingly replace it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r5.anchor: ولب تلك البزور شديد الحرارة يلدغ اللسان والجلد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r6.claim: A parallel in al-Anbiyā’ says that even a mustard seed’s weight is brought forth, reinforcing the same point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r6.anchor: وتقدم نظير هذا في سورة الأنبياء فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r7.claim: The heavens are coordinated with the rock as a more inaccessible location, and earth is added to include all terrestrial places; any location is equally within God’s knowledge and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p162/r7.anchor: لأن الصخرة من أجزاء الأرض فذكر بعدها { أو في السماوات }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir explains that the intervening verses belong among Luqman's counsels to his son, accounting for their placement within the account of his advice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن جرير وجه اعتراض هذه الآيات بين الخبرين عن وصية لقمان أن هذا مما أوصى به لقمان ابنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the son asked whether God would know of a seed lying at the bottom of the sea; Luqman answered with this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r2.anchor: أن ابن لقمان قال لأبيه أرأيت لو كانت حبة في قعر البحر أكان الله يعلمها فأجابه بهذه الآية قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says the son asked how God could know about a sin committed where no one could see him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r3.anchor: أنه قال يا أبت إن عملت الخطيئة حيث لا يراني أحد كيف يعلمها الله فأجابه بهذا قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r4.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r4.claim: Nafi alone reads miṯqāl with the lām in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده مثقال حبة برفع اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the nominative reading with feminine tak by taking a mustard-seed weight as referring to a single mustard seed, equivalent to if it is a seed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج من قرأ برفع المثقال مع تأنيث تك فلأن مثقال حبة من خردل راجع إلى معنى خردلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r6.claim: For the other construction, al-Zajjaj gives the sense either as the thing the son asked about or as any human deed, however small, that God will bring forth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ مثقال حبة فعلى معنى إن التي سألتني عنها إن تك مثقال حبة وعلى معنى إن فعلة الإنسان وإن صغرت يأت بها الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r7.claim: Qatada identifies the rock as a mountain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى فتكن في صخرة قال قتادة في جبل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies it as the rock beneath the seventh earth, outside both the heavens and the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r8.anchor: وقال السدي هي الصخرة التي تحت الأرض السابعة ليست في السماوات ولا في الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r9.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r9.claim: Abu Malik takes God's bringing it forth to mean that God knows it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r9.anchor: أحدها يعلمها الله قاله أبو مالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes God's bringing it forth to mean making it manifest.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r11.claim: A third interpretation is that God brings the deed forth for its recompense in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r11.anchor: والثالث يأت بها الله في الآخرة للجزاء عليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains subtlety as God's ability to extract the deed and knowledge as awareness of its location.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج لطيف باستخراجها خبير بمكانها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r13.claim: The seed's weight is an example of people's deeds: God will produce them on Judgment Day, as stated in the closing lines of al-Zalzala.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p320#2/r13.anchor: وهذا مثل لأعمال العباد والمراد أن الله تعالى يأتي بأعمالهم يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the pronoun most likely refers to an injustice or sin as tiny as a mustard seed; some instead read it as the pronoun of the situation, with mithqal nominative on that reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r1.anchor: أي: إن المظلمة أو الخطيئة لو كانت مثقال حبة [من] (5) خردل. وجوز بعضهم أن يكون الضمير في قوله: {إنها} ضمير الشأن والقصة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r2.claim: On Judgment Day God brings the deed forth when the just scales are set and repays good with good and evil with evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: {يأت بها الله} أي: أحضرها الله يوم القيامة حين يضع الموازين القسط، وجازى عليها إن خيرا فخير،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r3.claim: God’s subtle knowledge means nothing escapes Him, however tiny; He is aware even of an ant’s movement in deep night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r3.anchor: أي: لطيف العلم، فلا تخفى عليه الأشياء وإن دقت ولطفت وتضاءلت {خبير} بدبيب النمل في الليل البهيم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi relates, through a route from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions if sound, that the rock is beneath the seven earths; similar views are attributed to Atiyya, Abu Malik, al-Thawri, and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r4.anchor: ذكره السدي بإسناده ذلك المطروق عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وجماعة من الصحابة إن صح ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the under-seven-earths report likely Israelite material, neither affirmed nor denied; the apparent meaning is that God exposes even a speck hidden in solid rock.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر -والله أعلم -أن المراد: أن هذه الحبة في حقارتها لو كانت داخل صخرة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r6.claim: Abu Said al-Khudri reports the Prophet saying that if someone acted in a solid rock with no opening, his deed would still come out to people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p337#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r1.claim: مثقال حبة is read in the accusative or nominative; with the accusative, the pronoun refers to a tiny good or evil deed, even if hidden in an inaccessible place, which God brings for its agent’s reckoning on Judgment Day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r1.anchor: قرىء { مثقال حبة } بالنصب والرفع ، فمن نصب كان الضمير للهنة من الإساءة أو الإحسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r2.claim: With the nominative reading, the pronoun is a pronoun of the situation; مثقال is feminine because it is annexed to حبة, as in the cited poetic line.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ بالرفع : كان ضمير القصة ، وإنما أنث المثقال لإضافته إلى الحبة ، كما قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r3.claim: God’s subtlety means His knowledge reaches every hidden thing, and His expertise means He knows its full reality.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r3.anchor: إن الله لطيف } يتوصل علمه إلى كل خفي { خبير } عالم بكنهه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r4.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r4.claim: Qatāda explains لطيف as able to extract the seed and خبير as knowing where it rests.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة : لطيف باستخراجها ، خبير بمستقرها .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r5.speaker: ابن لقمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r5.claim: Ibn Luqmān asks whether God knows a seed in the depths of the sea; Luqmān says God knows the smallest hidden things, and a seed in rock is more concealed than one in water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r5.anchor: وروي أن ابن لقمان قال له : أرأيت الحبة تكون في مقل البحر أي : في مغاصه يعلمها الله ؟ فقال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r6.claim: Another explanation identifies the rock as the one beneath the earth, called Sijjīn, where unbelievers’ deeds are recorded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r6.anchor: وقيل : الصخرة هي التي تحت الأرض ، وهي السجين يكتب فيها أعمال الكفار .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r7.claim: فتكن is also read with kasra on the kāf, from وَكَنَ الطائر يَكِنُ, meaning it settled in its nighttime roost.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p502/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( فتكن ) بكسر الكاف . من وكن الطائر يكن : إذا استقر في وكنته

MUJAHID:v2p504#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p504#3/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MUJAHID:v2p504#3/r1.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya explains God as subtle in extracting even a tiny hidden thing and fully aware of its location.
MUJAHID:v2p504#3/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس عن أبي العالية في قوله ﴿ إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير ﴾ قال لطيف باستخراجها خبير بمكانها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.speaker: مدني والباقون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.claim: Madani reads mithqālu in the nominative, with the pronoun referring to the story; the other readers use the accusative, taking the pronoun as the deed of wrong or right.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.anchor: بالرفع مدنى والضمير للقصة وأنث المثقال لإضافته إلى الحبة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.claim: The nominative reading makes kāna a complete verb; in the accusative reading it is copular and the pronoun refers to the act of good or evil, as small as a mustard seed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.anchor: والباقون بالنصب والضمير للهيئة من الإساءة والإحسان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.claim: The author cites an unnamed poetic line as evidence for feminine agreement when the masculine noun is annexed to the feminine word ḥabba.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.anchor: كما قال كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.claim: Even a tiny deed hidden in a rock's core or anywhere in the upper or lower world will be brought by God; most interpreters identify the rock with Sijjīn, where evil deeds are recorded, outside the earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.anchor: أى فكانت مع صغرها فى أخفى موضع وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة أو حيث كانت فى العالم العلوى أو السفلى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.claim: God brings the deed forth on the Day of Resurrection and holds its agent to account.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r6.claim: Laṭīf means either that God's knowledge reaches every hidden thing or that He is gentle in extracting it; Khabīr means He knows its true nature or its location.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#2/r6.anchor: عالم بكنهه أو لطيف باستخراجها خبير بمستقرها

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r1.claim: Luqmān addresses his son to teach him the extent of God’s power in terms he can grasp; the mustard seed is too slight for the senses to register on a scale.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r1.anchor: المعنى: وقال لقمان لابنه يا بني. وهذا القول من لقمان إنما قصد به إعلام ابنه بقدر قدرة الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r2.claim: Even a mustard-seed measure of provision hidden in these places is brought by God to its recipient; do not let anxiety over provision distract you from duties and following the path of one who turns to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r2.anchor: أي لو كان للإنسان رزق مثقال حبة خردل في هذه المواضع جاء الله بها حتى يسوقها إلى من هي رزقه

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r3.claim: The author connects this lesson with the Prophet’s advice to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd not to worry excessively: what is destined and provided will reach you.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r3.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعبد الله بن مسعود: «لا تكثر همك ما يقدر يكون وما ترزق يأتيك»

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r4.claim: The verse declares that God encompasses everything in knowledge and has counted all things; He has no partner.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r4.anchor: وقد نطقت هذه الآية بأن الله تعالى قد أحاط بكل شيء علما، وأحصى كل شيء عددا سبحانه لا شريك له.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r5.speaker: ابن لقمان
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r5.claim: A report says Luqmān’s son asked whether God would know of a seed fallen to the bottom of the sea, and Luqmān answered with this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r5.anchor: وروي أن ابن لقمان سأل أباه عن الحبة تقع في سفل البحر أيعلمها الله؟ فراجعه لقمان بهذه الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r6.claim: Another interpretation applies the seed-sized thing to good or sinful deeds: God brings them forth, so none of a person’s destined actions escape; this combines hope and fear, unlike the provision reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنه أراد الأعمال، المعاصي والطاعات أي إن تك الحسنة أو الخطيئة مثقال حبة يأت بها الله

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r7.claim: Mithqāl ḥabbah can describe a physical substance’s measure or, by analogy, the measure of a deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r7.anchor: عبارة تصلح للجواهر، أي قدر حبة وتصلح للأعمال أي ما يزنه على جهة المماثلة قدر حبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r8.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r8.claim: ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī reads فتكن with kasra on kāf and a doubled nūn, deriving it from al-kinn, a covered thing; this supports the physical-object reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r8.anchor: ومما يؤيد قول من قال هي من الجواهر: قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري «فتكن» بكسر الكاف وشد النون، من الكن الذي هو الشيء المغطى.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r9.speaker: جمهور القراء
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r9.claim: The majority read in tak with feminine tāʾ and mithqāla accusative as kāna’s predicate; its implicit subject is estimated as your question, or sin and obedience under the deeds interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r9.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء: «إن تك» بالتاء من فوق «مثقال» بالنصب على خبر كان، واسمها مضمر تقديره: مسألتك

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r10.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r10.claim: A report says the son asked how God could know of a sin committed unseen; Luqmān answered with the verse, and the son trembled until he died.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r10.anchor: فما زال ابنه يضطرب حتى مات قاله مقاتل.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r11.claim: In inna-hā, the pronoun refers to the matter or story, as in It is the story that Hind is standing; Basrans allow this construction, while Kūfans restrict it to feminine wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r11.anchor: والضمير في «إنها» ضمير القصة كقولك: إنها هند قائمة أي القصة إنها إن تك مثقال حبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r12.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ reads mithqālu in the nominative; tak then refers to a mustard seed, meaning if it is a mustard seed.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع: «مثقال» بالرفع، وعلى هذا «تك» يرجع إلى معنى خردلة أي إن تك حبة من خردل.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r13.claim: Another grammatical account lets the feminine verb agree semantically with the feminine thing added to mithqāl, whether a good or bad deed; 6:160 similarly uses feminine agreement for the good deeds meant.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16/r13.anchor: وقيل: أسند إلى المثقال فعلا فيه علامة التأنيث من حيث انضاف إلى مؤنث هو منه لأن مثقال الحبة من الخردل إما سيئة أو حسنة كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r1.claim: The author cites 6:160 to show feminine agreement when the intended referent is good deeds, then illustrates the construction with an unnamed poet’s line.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r1.anchor: فله عشر أمثالها [الأنعام: 160] فأنث وإن كان المثل مذكرا لأنه أراد الحسنات.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r2.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates feminine agreement; the source does not name its poet.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r3.claim: Here tak means to occur, so it does not require a predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r3.anchor: و«تك» هاهنا بمعنى تقع فلا تقتضي خبرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r4.claim: One explanation treats the rock as an emphatic extreme: God’s power reaches what lies inside a rock as well as what is in heaven and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r4.anchor: قيل: معنى الكلام المبالغة والانتهاء في التفهيم أي أن قدرته تعالى تنال ما يكون في تضاعيف صخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās locates the rock below the seven earths, with the earth resting on it.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الصخرة تحت الأرضين السبع وعليها الأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r6.claim: Another view places the rock on the back of the fish.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي الصخرة على ظهر الحوت.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r7.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says the rock lies outside the heavens and earth, beyond seven earths, with an angel standing on it; he notes the heavens and earth already encompass everything else.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: هي صخرة ليست في السموات والأرض، بل هي وراء سبع أرضين عليها ملك قائم

QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r8.claim: The author says al-Suddī’s location is possible, but the rock clause may instead reinforce the point like the repeated creation wording in 96:1–2 and the night journey wording in 17:1.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:16#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله ممكن، ويمكن أن يقال: قوله: { فتكن في صخرة } تأكيد كقوله:
